articles.title: Pacers' Tyrese Haliburton Claps Back at Bucks Fan After Throwing Out 1st Pitch at Cubs Game
articles.summary: Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton took some time to push back against a fan who criticized him for throwing out a first pitch for the Chicago Cubs despite growing up as a Milwaukee Brewers fan.
articles.body:
Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton took some time to push back against a fan who criticized him for throwing out a first pitch for the Chicago Cubs despite growing up as a Milwaukee Brewers fan.

Haliburton responded to a post criticizing him of "going out of his way" to root against Milwaukee by screenshotting previous posts from the same user praising his play.

Winners and Losers from Clippers Ruling 📊

The social media spat took place after Haliburton made a Thursday night appearance at Wrigley Field ahead of the Cubs' 2-1 win over the visiting Brewers.

Haliburton said in an April 2025 appearance on the Pat McAfee Show he was no longer a Brewers fan because the club had rescinded an invitation to throw out a ceremonial first pitch in 2024.

At that time, the Pacers had just eliminated the Milwaukee Bucks from a second consecutive first round of the NBA playoffs.

The clubs avoided the same matchup last season by both falling short of the playoffs as Haliburton sat out the campaign with the Achilles injury he suffered during the 2025 NBA Finals.

Haliburton is now preparing to make his comeback after more than a year away when the Pacers open the regular season Oct. 21 at the New Orleans Pelicans.

articles.title: NBA 2K27 predicts the season: LeBron's shocking start with 76ers, a new MVP and an NBA Finals rematch
articles.summary: For the third year in a row, Yahoo Sports is simulating a full NBA season in the latest entry in the NBA 2K franchise — NBA 2K27.
articles.body:
For the third year in a row, Yahoo Sports is simulating a full NBA season in the latest entry in the NBA 2K franchise — NBA 2K27.

Last year's simulation proved to be shockingly accurate. Not only did NBA 2K26 predict the Knicks to win the NBA Finals and Jalen Brunson to be named NBA Finals MVP, it also nailed Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's repeat bid for MVP, Victor Wembanyama's Defensive Player of the Year nod and Cooper Flagg's Rookie of the Year victory. It even had the Wizards as the league's worst team, albeit with half of the wins the real-life version managed to muster.

All things considered, it was safe to say one of the best simulation video game experiences on the market walked the walk.

For those new to this series, here are the rules: We select one team, at random (Miami Heat) and run through a MyEras season with CPU trade offers turned off, with G-League, scouting and rotational decisions set to automatic. The simulation is halted to record the NBA Cup winner, at the end of the regular season and before the NBA Finals.

(Disclaimer: Although the NBA has ruled in the Kawhi Leonard-Clippers investigation, Leonard's trade to the Raptors remains in limbo, so for this simulation he is still a member of the Clippers roster.)

Much like last year, before the simulation fully got underway, we were prompted that LeBron James would be retiring — despite signing a two-year deal with the Sixers — and offered the option to have him do a retirement tour.

Since we'd be simulating everything anyway, we declined.

That housekeeping item aside, there's no way to sugarcoat how James' first — and perhaps only — season with the Sixers went, according to NBA 2K27. In what will wind up being his age-42 season, James played 77 games and finished with career lows in minutes per game (30.5), points (16.9) and assists (4.9). Even his rebounding average (5.6) was the lowest total since his rookie season.

If James' struggles weren't enough of a surprise, the revamped Sixers were the biggest shocker of the entire simulation, and not in a good way. Philadelphia, after adding James and trading for Jaylen Brown, finished 14th in the Eastern Conference with a record of 27-55. Brown's scoring took a major dip, dropping more than seven points per game, and his scoring (21.5) and assist (3.3) averages were the lowest since the 2019-20 season.

Injuries did not play a major role in Philadelphia's nightmare season, as only Tyrese Maxey missed significant time (20 games) of the projected starting lineup of Brown, James, Maxey, VJ Edgecombe and Joel Embiid.

Considering the talent and level of expectations surrounding the 76ers, this was easily the least feasible outcome of anything that happened in the 2K27 simulation.

No, it wasn't the Mavs for a third consecutive year.

This time, the NBA's best record belonged to the Minnesota Timberwolves, who reloaded their roster in an attempt to surround Anthony Edwards with a championship-caliber supporting cast during his prime.

In NBA 2K27, the experiment worked, as Minnesota finished with the best record in the NBA (63-19), with Chris Finch taking home Coach of the Year honors. The Wolves finished as a top-3 team in both offense and defense, and the pairing of Edwards and LaMelo Ball was lethal. Ant-Man finished second in the league in scoring (29 PPG) and Ball was fifth in assists (7.5 APG).

The Bucks were the NBA's worst squad, which shouldn't come as a huge surprise considering the heavy rebuild in the wake of the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade this offseason. Milwaukee finished 24-58 and had a bottom-10 squad on both the offensive and defensive sides of the ball.

GTA VI isn't the only hotly anticipated, Miami-related debut this fall, as Antetokounmpo is set to play for a non-Bucks team for the first time in his career.

Unfortunately for Antetokounmpo and the Heat, things did not start off well. Before the month of November was over, Antetokounmpo (right hand fracture), Tim Hardaway Jr. (broken ankle), and Bam Adebayo (twisted knee) were all shelved for multiple weeks. Bobby Portis would suffer a season-ending knee injury in February.

Despite all of the injuries, Miami did manage to make the playoffs, finishing 38-44, good for the ninth seed in the Eastern Conference, and Antetokounmpo was named the NBA's Clutch Player of the Year, finishing with 21.7 points per game, 11.1 rebounds, 5.6 assists and 2.9 stocks.

Miami was ousted in the first round of the play-in tournament by the Bulls.

The in-season tournament final featured the defending Cup and NBA champion Knicks against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Led by NBA Cup MVP Gilgeous-Alexander, the Thunder took down the Knicks in what would be an ominous sign for New York.

Most Valuable Player — Although Gilgeous-Alexander led the NBA in scoring (31.9 PPG), the Victor Wembanyama Era officially got underway in NBA 2K27. Wembanyama — who won Defensive Player of the Year in the simulation as well — finished the season averaging 25 points per game, 13.1 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 4.9 stocks. While Wembanyama will continue to face stiff competition from both Gilgeous-Alexander and Nikola Jokić in the MVP race, this feels like more of an inevitability for the 22-year-old, assuming he stays healthy.

Rookie of the Year — Memphis' Cameron Boozer edged No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa to become the second consecutive Duke player to win the award. Boozer finished with averages of 13.5 points and 7.7 rebounds for the Grizzlies, while Dybantsa averaged 10.8 and 4.9 in the same categories for the Wizards.

Coach of the Year — Chris Finch, Timberwolves

Defensive Player of the Year — Victor Wembanyama, Spurs

Sixth Man of the Year — Jalen Green, Suns

Most Improved Player — Zaccharie Risacher, Mavericks

Clutch Player of the Year — Giannis Antetokounmpo, Heat

The NBA 2K franchise must really love the Knicks, because for the third year in a row, New York is playing for the (simulated) Larry O'Brien trophy. The Knicks finished with the second seed in the Eastern Conference and marched through the bracket, with Jalen Brunson winning East Finals MVP by averaging 31.3 points per game. Waiting for him on the other side was a familiar foe.

San Antonio, led by league MVP Wembanyama, took down the No. 1 seed Timberwolves in the West finals, with Wembanyama adding to his trophy case in the process.

In the rematch of the actual NBA Finals from last year, the script was flipped entirely, with the Spurs sweeping the Knicks in dominant fashion. In Game 2 and Game 4, Wembanyama finished with 20-plus rebounds and had an astonishing eight blocks in the closeout game. Wembanyama finished the series averaging 26.5 points, 18.2 rebounds, 5.3 assists and seven stocks, earning the Bill Russell NBA Finals MVP Award.

If Wembanyama were to win NBA MVP, be named Defensive Player of the Year and capture the NBA Finals MVP Award, he would join Hakeem Olajuwon as the only players in NBA history to do so in the same season.

articles.title: Ben Simmons reportedly agrees to 1-year, $3.5M deal with Kings
articles.summary: The 30-year-old Simmons did not play in the NBA last season.
articles.body:
Ben Simmons is returning to the NBA after reportedly signing a one-year, $3.5 million contract to join the Sacramento Kings, according to ESPN's Marc Spears and Shams Charania .

He is expected to be a backup point guard for rookie Darius Acuff Jr.

The 30-year-old Simmons last played in the NBA during the 2024-25 season with the Los Angeles Clippers. After his contract expired following that season, he did not sign anywhere in free agency and reportedly turned down a one-year minimum contract offer from the New York Knicks.

Simmons had a productive first four NBA seasons with the Philadelphia 76ers, where he won Rookie of the Year and averaged double-digits in points. The 2021-22 season saw him hold out and ask to be traded, which led to a move to the Brooklyn Nets.

Back injuries limited Simmons' time on the court in Brooklyn and he eventually underwent surgery for a herniated disc. He was waived by the Nets in Feb. 2025 and had his contract bought out. Two days later, he signed with the Clippers.

As his NBA future remained in limbo, Simmons was a full participant at a player-led minicamp for the Australian men's basketball team in August with the 2028 Olympics in his sights.

Not long after that camp, Simmons worked out for Kings general manager Scott Perry in Miami and later flew to Sacramento to visit with head coach Doug Christie and his staff.

Simmons kept busy last season, just not focused solely on basketball. He purchased a controlling stake in the South Florida Sails Angling Club , a professional sports fishing team. In May, the team won the 2026 SFC Walker's Cay Open Championship .

The 2016 No. 1 overall pick in the NBA Draft is a three-time All-Star and two-time All-Defensive First Team selection. Over 383 career games, he's averaged 13.1 points, 7.4 rebounds, 7.2 assists, and 1.5 steals per game.

articles.title: El Mundial arranca con récord de un rival de España: 20 triples para Japón con nueve de Hayashi
articles.standfirst: La selección japonesa supera a Mali por 102-97 en el partido inaugural
articles.summary: La selección japonesa supera a Mali por 102-97 en el partido inaugural
articles.body: El Mundial Femenino arrancó con récord en un partido que enfrentó a los dos siguientes rivales de España. En el partido inaugural del torneo, Japón se impuso a Mali por un apretado 102-97. La selección asiática confirmó su fama de equipo tirador y anotó 20 triples, nueve de ellos de Saki Hayashi. Las dos marcas son topes en el campeonato. Japón igualó el mejor registro en la historia del Mundial Femenino. Lo poseía ella misma desde que en 1994 también hiciera 20 triples en un encuentro frente a Kenia. Hayashi, mientras, superó los ocho aciertos en los que estaba el techo en poder de la surcoreana Beon Yeon-Ha (2002) y de la cubana Gricel Herrera Méndez (1998). La escolta nipona, sin embargo, no se mostró del todo satisfecha con su actuación, finalizada con 27 puntos tras hacer 9/15 desde el arco. "Obviamente, estoy contenta, pero mi trabajo es simplemente tirar. En el vestuario se da por hecho que voy a tirar triples. Sin embargo, anoté nueve, pero fallé los dos primeros. Tengo que volver a trabajar", dijo. Su seleccionador Corey Gaines se deshizo en elogios hacia ella: "He entrenado en la WNBA y la NBA, he jugado en la FIBA y la Euroliga y no juzgo a una jugadora hasta que la veo entrenar todos los días. He visto a 'Kiki' durante muchos años y es una de las mejores tiradoras que he visto". Por supuesto, a golpe de triple, Japón acabó con la resistencia de Mali, que será el rival de España en la mañana de este sábado. Las africanas llegaron a tener 10 puntos de renta en el tercer periodo (61-71), gracias al poderío interior de Aminata Sangaré (22 puntos con 9/9 en tiros de dos y ocho rebotes) y Sika Kone (21+11, siete ofensivos). Pero su última ventaja fue a falta de 4:41 para el final (84-85). Ahí el partido se redujo al acierto exterior de las japonesas contra el dominio de Sangaré en la zona. La pívot hizo 10 puntos casi seguidos para mantener las opciones de su equipo, pero un acierto de Maki Takada a falta de 48 segundos fue determinante (101-95). En la última posesión, Mali atrapó cinco rebotes en ataque pero fue incapaz de anotar y apretar aún más el marcador.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown's GoPro Found at Bottom of Ocean by USA Swimmers Patrick Sammon, Michael Andrew
articles.summary: Team USA swimmers Patrick Sammon and Michael Andrew say they didn't recognize Jaylen Brown when reviewing footage of the Philadelphia 76ers star on a GoPro they found on the ocean floor in Hawaii.
articles.body:
Team USA swimmers Patrick Sammon and Michael Andrew say they didn't recognize Jaylen Brown when reviewing footage of the Philadelphia 76ers star on a GoPro they found on the ocean floor in Hawaii.

Sammon launched their search for the lost camera's owner by sharing footage of Brown paddling on a surfboard and asking followers to help identify him.

"As soon as we turned it on, we were like, 'Oh, this guy looks super familiar,'" Sammon said in an interview shared Friday by USA Swimming. "This guy is, like, seven feet tall, and there's a mic boom over his head, so you could see he has a full-on camera crew. And we're like, 'Alright, we've got to figure out who this guy is.'"

The swimmers' discovery quickly went viral after Sammon posted the video of Brown in late August.

"Anyone know who this is? Tag him if you do," Sammon wrote on the video. "Help me find him so I can give him his footage back + a free swim lesson lol."

Sammon said he received responses within the first two minutes of posting asking him if he really didn't know the video featured Brown.

Should Brown take Sammon up on his offer of lessons, it wouldn't be his first time learning from a professional. He said last October he had been recently taught by former U.S. Olympic swimmer and Boston College swim coach Dara Torres.

articles.title: USA vs. China Box Score, Reaction from 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup Group Ahead of KO Bracket
articles.summary: Team USA got its title defense off to an impressive start Friday at the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, defeating China 94-61 in its opening game of group play.
articles.body:
Team USA got its title defense off to an impressive start Friday at the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, defeating China 94-61 in its opening game of group play.

Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers, Rhyne Howard and Jackie Young all scored in double figures for the Americans in what was a one-sided affair.

Making her FIBA World Cup debut, Clark was the standout for the United States, as the Indiana Fever star was the only American to post a double-double with 14 points and 11 assists.

Clark, who came off the bench, had just five points at halftime, but they were of the impressive variety, as she absorbed contact to make a layup and drilled a long three-pointer:

She truly hit her stride during the second half, helping Team USA balloon its 20-point halftime lead to 33 by the end of the game.

Clark looked the part of the United States' best player on Friday, and she garnered plenty of praise on social media because of it:

As excellent as Clark's performance was, the even more encouraging takeaway from Friday's game for the U.S. may have been its smothering team defense.

The Americans held China to just 32 percent shooting from the field and 26 percent shooting from beyond the arc. Team USA also forced 16 turnovers.

That style of play figures to serve the United States well regardless of who it plays in Berlin, as the Americans look to win their fifth consecutive FIBA Women's World Cup.

They will return to action Sunday for another Group D game against Italy before finishing group play Monday against Czechia.

Assuming Team USA wins Group D as expected, it will begin knockout round action on Thursday.

articles.title: España - Alemania en directo | Mundial de baloncesto femenino 2026 hoy en vivo
articles.summary: 15 asistencias para España por 2 de Alemania en los primeros 20 minutos. Una bestialidad. Se quedó Iyana con un cómodo tiro, pero no pudo anotar. Perf
articles.body:
Última hora del España - Alemania en directo:

¡¡¡Muy buenas tardes y bienvenidos a todos y todas al Mundial Femenino de Baloncesto 2026 de Alemania !!! La selección española realiza su debut en este primer día de torneo ante la anfitriona , con toda la ilusión por conseguir algo grande este verano. Tras perderse la última cita mundialista, España regresa a todo lo grande con un equipo de absoluta garantía y entre las que figuran cinco jugadoras de la WNBA , por primera vez en su historia. María Conde , Raquel Carrera , Awa Fam , Alicia Flórez y Megan Gustafson viajaron desde el otro lado del charco para sumarse al resto de las jugadores que completan la convocatoria: Paula Ginzo , Helena Pueyo , Mariona Ortiz , Alba Torrens , Maite Cazorla , además de Elena Buenavida e Iyana Martín , que se podrían incorporar también en breves a la liga norteamericana.

Las de Miguel Méndez llegan a este Mundial tras un 3-2 en la clasificación, con victorias sobre Puerto Rico , Senegal y Nueva Zelanda , y dos derrotas ante Italia y Estados Unidos, la máxima favorita para levantar su decimosegundo trofeo. Sin embargo, respecto a los partidos previos para preparar este campeonato, España ha hecho un pleno. Cuatro victorias contra, precisamente, Alemania , Nigeria , Bélgica y Mali , quien también queda encuadrada en el grupo A, además de Japón.

Más allá de los Mundiales , España viene recientemente de conseguir dos platas consecutivas en los Eurobasket 23 y 25 después de perder ambas finales ante su verdugo, Bélgica. En los Juegos Olímpicos de París 2024 también cayó ante las europeas, en cuartos de final . Y esta rivalidad no entiende de competiciones; en el último Mundial que disputó España , ganó el partido por el tercer y cuarto puesto a las belgas para colgarse el bronce.

La Selección llega a este torneo con todas las expectativas, y sin miedo a nadie, como dejó claró su seleccionador : "La bendita inconsciencia hace que no temamos a nadie" , declaró a MARCA . También Iyana Martín y Awa Fam dijeron en una entrevista a este periódico que este equipo tan joven "se muere por ganar". Por lo pronto, FIBA pronostica al equipo nacional como tercera favorita para levantar la Copa del Mundo , sólo por detrás de Estados Unidos y Francia . Veremos qué nos tiene deparado esta Selección que pocas veces falla a su cita con el metal , en un torneo que apenas dura 10 días , con la final el próximo domingo 13 de septiembre . Aquí viviremos todos los partidos de España , y hoy te acompañamos para vivir el primero de ellos. Desde las 17:45 , contra Alemania y, como siempre, en MARCA .

articles.title: Inside a Louisiana courtroom': SEC-LSU legal circus played out like a John Grisham novel in stunning showdown
articles.summary: Greg Sankey snuck into a Baton Rouge courtroom as the SEC filed a bombshell federal lawsuit against LSU and Lane Kiffin over eligibility rules.
articles.body: BATON ROUGE, La. — SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey covertly arrived at a Louisiana courtroom Thursday morning more than an hour before the circus was scheduled to begin, just two days before LSU was set to welcome Clemson to "Death Valley.," Around the same time Sankey took his seat, Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill stepped out of a government vehicle and made her way inside. Before entering, however, she made her allegiance clear. LSU MIGHT HAVE TO SUE THE SEC IF THIS LEGAL WAR IS EXPEDITED, WHILE DABO SWINNEY IS STAYING IN HIS 'LANE' "Go Tigers," Murrill, wearing a purple outfit, proclaimed before blasting both the NCAA and SEC If you didn’t realize the courthouse was just minutes from LSU’s campus, the purple-and-gold atmosphere inside and outside the building made it clear. SEC LAWYERS, LANE KIFFIN AND DEATH VALLEY: COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S WEEK 1 IS SET FOR FIREWORKS Television cameras lined the street as reporters waited for everyone connected to the lawsuit to arrive for the highly anticipated showdown. While nearly everyone involved entered through the front door, Sankey slipped in through a side entrance, avoiding the cameras and reporters hoping to ask him questions. Why? The Baton Rouge Sheriff’s Office later released a statement saying Sankey used the side entrance because of threats made against the commissioner before his arrival. Some people associated with the plaintiffs, however, suggested the SEC leader was simply trying to avoid questions. All of that pregame commotion set the stage for what came next. And to put it mildly, Thursday’s hearing was dramatic. SEC drops a bombshell as Louisiana hearing gets underway The conference knew exactly what it was doing Thursday morning. If you thought Sankey traveled to Baton Rouge empty-handed, you haven’t been following the gamesmanship that unfolded behind the scenes in the days leading up to the hearing. Just minutes after Greg Sankey took a seat inside the witness box, a noticeable wave of emotions moved through the courtroom. It was in the early morning hours of Thursday that the Southeastern Conference had initiated a preemptive strike. The SEC had filed a federal lawsuit in Alabama against LSU, head coach Lane Kiffin and athletic department officials alleging that the school was violating First Amendment rights of the conference just as the hearing in Louisiana was getting underway. NCAA CREATED THIS MESS, NOW LSU SET TO MAKE DAE’QUAN WRIGHT COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S FIRST NFL RETURNEE The SEC’s lawsuit alleges that LSU was actively recruiting NFL players to return to college while also preventing the conference from enforcing its rules against professional athletes participating in collegiate sports. Simply put, the SEC is furious that LSU has challenged the conference’s attempts to enforce its eligibility rules for athletes returning from professional sports. NCAA HAS NO PLANS TO SURRENDER, AS ELIGIBILITY LAWSUITS FOR 2022 CLASS TURN INTO AN ALL-OUT LEGAL WAR "Did you authorize the SEC to sue LSU and coach Lane Kiffin?" attorney Tony Clayton asked Sankey. When asked why the conference took that step, Sankey pointed to the authority of the presidents and chancellors he represents. "We established our First Amendment right for freedom of association, so that our conference can make decisions and our members can make decisions about membership," Sankey said. The timing caught the plaintiffs off guard, with attorneys sharing the news amongst them at the table. Clayton asked Sankey three separate times about the conference suing one of its own members before Judge Will Jorden moved the proceedings along. Many expected the hearing to take at least an hour before producing any fireworks. Instead, the SEC’s lawsuit created chaos within minutes of Sankey taking the stand. It was evident that Louisiana court thought timing was too convenient At the core of the lawsuit were athletes such as Dae’Quan Wright, who spent more than 10 hours inside the crowded courtroom, and their argument that they were placed in this position because of the NCAA’s decision not to grandfather the 2022 class into its new eligibility rules. The NCAA recently adopted a five-years-to-play-five-seasons model. However, athletes who would otherwise be eligible under the new guidelines were not included. The dispute has become even more complicated because some members of the 2022 class pursued professional opportunities after exhausting their eligibility under the previous system. One of the central issues discussed Thursday was why the SEC created new guidelines in late August prohibiting athletes who had pursued professional careers from receiving another season of eligibility. The argument against allowing professional athletes to return to college is easy to understand. Most college sports fans would likely agree that a player who has signed with a professional team or participated in a professional training camp should not be allowed to return to the college ranks. However, Clayton used the timing of the SEC’s new guidelines to attack the conference’s position. He questioned whether the rules were created in response to Judge Jorden’s initial temporary restraining order in the case. "That was not re-establishing the rule," Greg Sankey said about the SEC's meeting just over 10 days ago in Brimingham. "The rule was the same rule before and after. The rule was there when I arrived in 2002...What was issued in the memo was consistent with the clarity that was understood by our sixteen universities, and if you have an individual on your roster under that policy, here's the accountability that will be applied." Most people would agree that the SEC’s policy came in response to the series of court orders allowing athletes with professional experience to return to college sports. The Big Ten had already issued similar guidelines before the SEC followed suit. But after listening to Jorden’s arguments before he granted the athletes an injunction, it was clear there was an undercurrent of concern that the conferences had coordinated their actions to undermine his initial ruling. That possibility, however subtle, may have helped drive the legal chaos that unfolded in Baton Rouge just 48 hours before LSU was scheduled to take the field. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Call it Louisiana politics or home-field advantage, but LSU now faces a decision about how to proceed Friday afternoon — a decision that will only heighten the hostile atmosphere around campus throughout the weekend. Now, everyone is waiting to see whether the Tigers will follow through on the chaotic effort to strengthen their roster before the season begins. Or, as we now call it in college athletics, another Friday afternoon courtroom decision.

articles.title: Cathy Engelbert to Retire as WNBA Commissioner at End of 2026
articles.summary: The WNBA announced Friday that commissioner Cathy Engelbert is retiring from her position at the end of 2026.
articles.body:
The WNBA announced Friday that commissioner Cathy Engelbert is retiring from her position at the end of 2026.

Engelbert, 61, was named the WNBA's first-ever commissioner in 2019, essentially replacing current NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum, who was the WNBA's interim president from 2018 to 2019.

5 reasons women's FIBA World Cup is must-see TV

In a statement regarding her decision to step away, Engelbert said, "After more than seven years at the WNBA and more than 40 total years in business, I have made the decision to retire as WNBA commissioner. In 2019, I had the privilege of being appointed the league's first commissioner and to lead a league with enormous potential yet untapped awareness and significant undervaluation. Over the years, it has been amazing to watch WNBA players thrive and lead the massive cultural surge around women's sports."

Engelbert has been a polarizing figure during her time as WNBA commissioner, but the growth the league has experienced under her leadership is undeniable.

The WNBA went from a 12-team league when her tenure started to what is soon to be an 18-team league with the additions of expansion teams in Cleveland, Detroit and Philadelphia from 2028 through 2030.

On top of that, the WNBA currently has $3.1 billion worth of media rights contracts, and the newest collective bargaining agreement, which was ratified in March, resulted in the first $1 million salaries for WNBA players, as well as revenue sharing, per ESPN's Alexa Philippou .

Despite her successes on the business side, Engelbert has been the subject of criticism from WNBA players at times for various reasons, including issues with officiating and poor player salaries and accommodations prior to the current CBA.

Last year, Minnesota Lynx superstar forward and WNBA Players Association vice president Napheesa Collier offered a scathing assessment of Engelbert.

"We have the best players in the world. We have the best fans in the world, but right now we have the worst leadership in the world," Collier said. "If I didn't know exactly what the job entailed, maybe I wouldn't feel this way, but unfortunately for them, I do. We serve a league that has shown they think championship coaches and Hall of Fame players are dispensable and that's fine. It's professional sports, but I will not stand quietly by and allow different standards to be applied at the league level."

It isn't yet known who will succeed Engelbert, but time is running short on her tenure.

Each team has only a handful of regular-season games remaining before the playoffs start this month. The WNBA Finals will then take place next month, signaling the end of the 2026 campaign.

By the time the 2027 WNBA draft is held in April, which is the first major event on the WNBA calendar next year, the league figures to be under new leadership.

articles.title: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert to retire at end of calendar year, ending controversial tenure
articles.summary: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert is retiring at the end of the calendar year. Englebert was the first-ever WNBA commissioner in league history, serving in the role for seven years.
articles.body: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert is retiring at the end of the calendar year. Engelbert was the first-ever WNBA commissioner in league history, serving in the role for seven years. The news was announced by NBA commissioner Adam Silver. "Cathy has presided over the WNBA through the most significant period of growth in the league’s 30-year history," Silver said in the WNBA’s statement. "We are grateful for Cathy’s leadership and unwavering commitment to the advancement of women’s basketball." articles.title: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert retiring at the end of this year
articles.summary: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert will retire at the end of this year, the league announced Friday.
articles.body: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert will retire at the end of this year, the league announced Friday. Engelbert, 61, has been the commissioner since July 2019. “I retire knowing we have built something bigger, stronger and more enduring than we could have imagined,” she said in a statement. “I am grateful to the WNBA and NBA team owners and staff, players, investors, fans and the powerhouse league office staff, who believed in what this league could become. I retire with immense gratitude and tremendous optimism for the future of the WNBA, with the best yet to come.” NBA Commissioner Adam Silver added, via his own statement: “Cathy has presided over the WNBA through the most significant period of growth in the league’s 30-year history. We are grateful for Cathy’s leadership and unwavering commitment to the advancement of women’s basketball.” Engelbert’s tenure has been marked by both massive growth for the league and tensions between players and the league office. Last September, Minnesota Lynx star Napheesa Collier blasted Engelbert, saying the WNBA had “the worst leadership in the world.” “The real threat to our league isn’t money,” Collier said at the time. “It isn’t ratings or even missed calls or even physical play. It’s the lack of accountability from the league office.” Collier’s comments came on the heels of growing frustration over the WNBA’s officiating, as well as in the midst of a contentious collective bargaining negotiation. The league and players didn’t agree to a new collective bargaining agreement until March of this year, and the agreement secured players $1 million salaries for the first time, and also introduced a new revenue-sharing model. Though Engelbert faced frequent criticisms from players and pundits, ranging from her handling of labor negotiations to the league’s response to culture war battles, she also presided over a boom period in the WNBA’s history. In 2024, the league signed a new television deal with Disney, Amazon and NBCUniversal reportedly worth $2.2 billion over 11 years. The WNBA has since added Paramount, Scripps, Versant and NBA TV as partners, bringing the total value of its TV rights to more than $3 billion. The WNBA is also expanding to 18 teams by 2030. After adding franchises in San Francisco (2025), Toronto (2026) and Portland (2026), the league will have teams in Cleveland (2028), Detroit (2029) and Philadelphia (2030) by the start of the next decade. Engelbert was named the WNBA’s first commissioner in 2019, as previous leaders of the league held only the title of president. She was challenged soon into her tenure, as the league had to hold its entire 2020 season in a bubble setting in Florida amid the Covid pandemic. The WNBA is currently in the middle of its 30th season, and appears to be continuing to grow. On Aug. 26, the game between the Caitlin Clark-led Indiana Fever and the Chicago Sky averaged 3.31 million viewers on NBC and Peacock, making it the league’s most-watched game since 1997, the WNBA’s inaugural season.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark impacta en su estreno en el Mundial ante la colosal Zhang Ziyu
articles.standfirst: La mediática base lidera con 14 puntos y 11 asistencias la paliza de Estados Unidos frente a China
articles.summary: La mediática base lidera con 14 puntos y 11 asistencias la paliza de Estados Unidos frente a China
articles.body: Estados Unidos llegó al Mundial Femenino rodeada de ciertas dudas. No por su dominio en los últimos campeonatos planetarios (69-0 desde 2006), sino por las importantes ausencias y el acercamiento de los rivales a su potencial. Pero en el estreno, la gran favorita no dio opción a China en la reedición de la final del último Mundial: 94-61. Buena manera de presentar sus credenciales. También lo hizo Caitlin Clark. La mediática base estadounidense debutó en un gran campeonato siendo la mejor de su selección. Sin llegar a deslumbrar, acabó con 14 puntos (3/7 en triples), 11 asistencias (tope en un estreno mundialista con EEUU) y 22 de valoración en 25 minutos. En el inicio de esta nueva era, otra de las jóvenes llamadas a liderarla, Paige Bueckers, hizo otros 14 puntos y cuatro asistencias después de despertar en la segunda mitad. Estados Unidos marcó territorio desde el inicio. Al final del primer cuarto ya mandaba por 27-14. China apretó en el segundo con un 0-9 para arrancar. La colosal Zhang Ziyu empezaba a imponer sus 2,20 metros, que la convirtieron en la jugadora más alta en la historia del Mundial. Hizo 13 puntos, aunque nueve de ellos llegaron desde el tiro libre. Añadió nueve rebotes. Pero las estadounidenses devolvieron el parcial y las rentas se fueron a los 20 puntos al descanso (49-29). Ya no hubo respuesta de China. Huérfana de su estrella, Li Yueru, que no ha podido estar en el Mundial tras perder el pasaporte, la selección asiática se resignó a la derrota. El doble-doble de Han Xu (11+10) fue muy poco ante el ataque coral de la gran favorita: Rhyne Howard sumó 14 puntos, Jackie Young 12 y la veterana Breanna Stewart añadió 7+7.

articles.title: WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert to retire after 2026 season
articles.summary: Engelbert was named commissioner ahead of the 2019 WNBA season.
articles.body:
WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert will retire at the end of the 2026 season, the league announced on Friday .

"After more than seven years at the WNBA and more than 40 total years in business, I have made the decision to retire as WNBA Commissioner," said Engelbert in a statement. "In 2019, I had the privilege of being appointed the league's first commissioner and to lead a league with enormous potential yet untapped awareness and significant undervaluation. Over the years, it has been amazing to watch WNBA players thrive and lead the massive cultural surge around women's sports."

Engelbert told The Associated Press that she felt the time was right to retire following the "financial transformation journey [the WNBA has] been on." She added that the decision was her own and she did not receive any pressure to step down.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

Engelbert was named the league's first-ever commissioner in May 2019 and has overseen two collective bargaining agreement negotiations and helped grow the league via a $3.1 billion media rights deal, as well as the addition of expansion teams. By 2030, the WNBA will have grown from 12 to 18 teams following the additions of franchises in San Francisco, Portland, Toronto, Cleveland, Detroit and Philadelphia.

Another feather in Engelbert's cap was the COVID-shortened 2020 season played in the "Wubble" at IMG Academy in Florida, avoiding the cancellation of the season amid the pandemic.

"Cathy has presided over the WNBA through the most significant period of growth in the league's 30-year history," said NBA commissioner Adam Silver in a statement. "We are grateful for Cathy's leadership and unwavering commitment to the advancement of women's basketball."

Silver had previously praised Engelbert's work but had been noncommittal about her future, while Engelbert was similarly evasive when asked directly about her plans at July's All-Star Game in Chicago.

Engelbert's tenure has not been without controversy. She was notably criticized over the last year by multiple players calling out her leadership. Napheesa Collier of the Minnesota Lynx said during last year's playoffs that under Engelbert, the league had the "worst leadership in the world." Nneka Ogwumike, head of the WNBA players' union, told ESPN she agreed with Collier's assessment.

While players cooled on their direct criticism of Engelbert after the new CBA was agreed to, the league continues to face challenges as it grows. Among other things, the next commissioner will be faced with addressing the transgender athlete issue that has permeated discussion around the league.

The WNBA has not announced who will succeed the 61-year-old Engelbert as commissioner. She told the AP she has been working on a succession plan for the past year, which will feature internal and external candidates.

"It's a good time to hand it off to the next leader to take the 'W' into a better phase," Engelbert said. "I'm proud of the team we built and everything we accomplished. A leader knows when it's time to drop the mic and move on after building a powerhouse team in the league office."

articles.title: Walter made improper deal with Magic after buying Dodgers: report
articles.summary: Billionaire Mark Walter made an improper deal with business partner Earvin "Magic" Johnson after getting the NBA legend's help in purchasing baseball's Los A...
articles.body:
Billionaire Mark Walter made an improper deal with business partner Earvin "Magic" Johnson after getting the NBA legend's help in purchasing baseball's Los Angeles Dodgers, according to a report on Friday.

In an episode of "Pablo Torre Finds Out", the journalist who last year helped unveil wrongdoing by the NBA's Los Angeles Clippers claimed Walter made hidden arrangements in his $350 million sale of life insurance firm EquiTrust to Johnson, a deal that made Johnson a billionaire.

Sources cited by Torre said the 2015 transaction was repayment by Walter to Johnson for the retired Los Angeles Lakers star using his influence and high profile to help Walter's group win a 2012 bid to buy the Dodgers, who have won the World Series the past two years.

Walter is reportedly the subject of an FBI investigation that some of his firms made unreported affiliated investments, which could put Walter at risk of tax fraud.

Last month, Walter sold the Los Angeles Lakers NBA club for $12.5 billion to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner barely a year after purchasing it from the Buss family for $10 billion.

Walter, through his company TWG Global, said last month that the Dodgers purchase complied with all Major League Baseball rules and regulations and an outside law firm conducted an investigation that found no irregularities in the deal.

Walter's other sports holdings include a share of a holding company that controls English Premier League club Chelsea, France's Strasbourg football team, the Cadillac Formula One team, a professional women's ice hockey league and the Los Angeles Sparks of the Women's NBA.

Torre outlined his report in an appearance on the MSNOW television show "Money Power Politics" on Friday, calling Walter a "one-man stimulus for billionaires owning sports teams" and saying, "Magic Johnson is one of the key figures in this."

"He was sold one of these insurance companies by Mark Walter, his business partner. It made him a billionaire in the process," Torre said.

"They got to together buy and fund the Dodgers using, effectively, law of transitive property via what it means to borrow money, the nest eggs of the parents and grandparents of America who did not realize that this was happening.

"This would be OK if disclosed as a related party transaction... Turns out if America is a land where the rule of law matters, you got to report this. Disclose and tell us the truth because it's not just your money, it turns out he's borrowing against ours."

A year ago, Torre claimed the NBA Clippers and owner Steve Ballmer had improperly avoided league salary cap rules in paying star Kawhi Leonard through business deals with companies that had contracts with the team.

On Wednesday, after an independent investigation and nearly a year after the first report, the NBA pounded the Clippers with some of the harshest punishments in league history, fining the team $30 million and stripping it of five future first-round NBA Draft choices.

The NBA suspended Ballmer from all league and team activities for a year. In a statement, the Clippers vowed to fight the penalties, a challenge that likely means lawsuits against the NBA.
